chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he ate fish, would say: 'O Allah, bless us in it and replace it for us with something better than it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication recited by the Prophet when eating fish?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s specific etiquette (adab) regarding fish, a food source often discussed in Shia jurisprudence for its permissibility and ease of consumption. The supplication not only expresses gratitude but also invokes divine abundance, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating spiritual mindfulness into daily sustenance. It serves as a practical model for believers to transform mundane acts of eating into opportunities for spiritual elevation and reliance on Allah’s provision.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Whenever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> ate the meat, said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Bless for us in it, and Replace by it (something) better than it’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Nuh ibn Shu’ayb from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, when eating fish would say, ’O Lord, make it a blessing for us and change it for us with what is better.’”
